relationships.description: The experience state is a condition of the state machine that drives a particular view, linking that machine node to the surface on which it is observed without implying control or rendering.
relationships.evidence: The view's state machine definition or view spec lists the state by name among its states, or the state record carries a view reference.

relationships.description: The experience state is the source node of the outgoing transition, so control leaves this state along that edge when the transition's triggering UI event fires and its guard holds.
relationships.evidence: In the machine config (e.g. an XState `states.editing.on.SUBMIT` entry), the transition is declared under this state's `on` block or carries this state as its `from` value.

relationships.description: While the experience state is active, it dictates which of the view's components are enabled, disabled or hidden, constraining what the view presents and permits.
relationships.evidence: The state's definition contains enabled/disabled/hidden component lists keyed to component instances of the view, or the view's template conditionally gates controls on `state.matches('<state>')`.

relationships.description: The experience state can hand the experience off directly to another experience state of the same machine, making that target state the next active condition.
relationships.evidence: The machine config has a transition under the source state whose `target` names the destination state, or the state's on-enter action navigates to it.

relationships.description: When the experience state becomes active, it causes the view to be displayed in the configuration that state prescribes, such as a loading or error screen.
relationships.evidence: The component code switches on the current state and returns the view's component (e.g. `case 'error': return <ErrorView/>`), or the state spec names the view as its rendered surface.

relationships.description: The experience state is a concrete instance of one of the reusable state pattern's generic states, inheriting its role, transitions and semantics while adding context-specific details.
relationships.evidence: The state definition declares an `extends`/`pattern` reference to the state pattern and maps to one of the pattern's named states, e.g. a 'loading' state derived from the loading/success/error pattern.

relationships.description: Entering or exiting the experience state automatically fires the state action bound to its lifecycle hook, such as submitting a form on entering 'submitted'.
relationships.evidence: The state's `entry` or `exit` array in the machine config lists the action, or the state action record names this state and an on-enter/on-exit hook.

relationships.description: The experience state draws on the reusable action template to define one of its lifecycle side effects, supplying concrete parameter values for that template on this state.
relationships.evidence: The state's entry/exit action references the template by identifier with bound parameter values, e.g. `entry: [{ type: 'navigateTemplate', params: { to: '/done' } }]`.

notes: associated-with, governs and renders to ux.view overlap; governs (component enablement) is the meaningful one, and renders conflicts with the state being 'not a screen'. navigates-to between states duplicates transitions modeled via StateTransition. uses StateActionTemplate bypasses StateAction, which already instantiates templates; triggers StateAction suffices.
